 WTA Hong Kong Day 2 Predictions Including Sorana Cirstea vs Maria Timofeeva 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 Day 2 in Hong Kong is packed with eight matches, including an all-Australian encounter between Maddison Inglis and Maya Joint. This is also veteran Sorana Cirstea’s final tournament, and she enters as the top seed, facing a dangerous Maria Timofeeva. Will she make it past the first round? We at LWOT offer our predictions
 WTA Hong Kong Day 2 Predictions
 Talia Gibson vs Oleksandra Oliynykova
 Head–to–Head: First Meeting
 Talia Gibson arrives in Hong Kong riding the momentum of a breakout season. The 22-year-old Australian made the final in Singapore after reaching the quarterfinals in Osaka. Tokyo was bumpier, with Alexandra Eala beating her in round two, but the bigger picture is hard to argue with. A qualifier-turned-quarterfinalist at Indian Wells earlier this year, Gibson now sits at a career-high 36 in the rankings and is playing with the confidence of someone who knows she belongs.
 Oleksandra Oliynykova, by contrast, is running on empty. The Ukrainian missed the Japan Open last week after a straight-sets loss to Mai Hontama, her third straight defeat, and has won just four of 13 outdoor hard-court matches in 2026. Gibson is simply the sharper, more settled player on this surface, and she should have too much firepower for an opponent searching for her rhythm. Back Gibson to book her place in the next round.
 Prediction: Gibson in 2 
 Maddison Inglis vs Maya Joint
 Head–to–Head : Joint 1 – 0 Inglis
 Maddison Inglis arrives in Hong Kong in desperate need of a reset. The world No. 135’s best result of 2026 remains a Vancouver semi-final, and the Asian swing has offered little to build on. The Australian has the experience to turn things around, but she’ll need to find rhythm fast.
 Across the net stands a rival who has found hers. Maya Joint, 20, reached the Korea Open final in September, then battled through Tokyo qualifying last week to knock out Sorana Cirstea and Cristina Bucsa on the way to the quarter-finals. A rocky season is giving way to growing belief and consistency, and she holds a 1-0 head-to-head edge from their Brisbane meeting in December 2024. With four wins from her last five, Joint has the clear edge, and Inglis will have to play her best tennis of the year to stop her.
 Prediction: Joint in 2 
 Tennis – U.S. Open – Flushing Meadows, New York, United States – September 4, 2026 Australia’s Maya Joint in action during her first round match with Taiwan’s Chan Hao-ching against Venus Williams of the U.S. and Serena Williams of the U.S. REUTERS/Brendan Mcdermid 
 Paula Badosa vs Elena Pridankina
 Head–to–Head: First Meeting
 Elena Pridankina enters Hong Kong through the back door, a lucky loser after falling in the final round of qualifying. She took the first set against Himeno Sakatsume before the match slipped away in three, and the form line isn’t kind: ranked outside the top 200, she hasn’t gone past the quarter-finals at any event in 2026. A first-round date with a former world #2 is a steep ask for a player still searching for rhythm.
 Paula Badosa is the opposite kind of opponent, a proven big-stage performer chasing a strong finish to a frustrating season. She looked sharp in Guangzhou, before eventual champion Harriet Dart reversed a set deficit to win 3-6 6-2 6-4 and halt her run in the quarter-finals. That loss will sting, but her runner-up finish at the Iasi Open this summer shows what she can still do when her game clicks. I expect Badosa to have far too much quality here, and Pridankina will need a career-best day to turn this into a contest.
 Prediction: Badosa in 2 
 Sorana Cirstea vs Maria Timofeeva
 Head–to–Head: First Meeting
 Sorana Cirstea heads into the final tournament of her career as the top seed in Hong Kong, carrying a season worth celebrating. There was the title on home soil in Cluj-Napoca, where she dismantled Emma Raducanu in the final, plus a first Roland Garros quarterfinal since 2009 and a run to the last four in Madrid. The form has cooled lately, though. Early exits in Ningbo and Tokyo suggest the 36-year-old is running on fumes, and a farewell tour is rarely kind to rhythm.
 That opens the door for Maria Timofeeva, who arrives with four lower-tier titles this year, including the Istanbul WTA 125. She was sharp in Guangzhou last week, beating Teodora Kostovic in straight sets before pushing Sun Xinran to the wire in a tight second-round loss.
 Cirstea still has the ranking, the pedigree, and the crowd’s goodwill, and she should be expected to win. But Timofeeva is match-fit, confident and has nothing to lose, which makes her the kind of awkward opponent a top seed doesn’t want in a farewell run, but she will want to avoid a first-round loss here.
 Prediction: Cirstea in 3
